reason: The new counted claim requires one sequence of finite Markovization sets to work for an uncountable time family without continuity or non-atomicity assumptions. Individual pairwise compactness and the previously examined ordinary concatenation continuity do not suffice. The proof combines monotone level-kernel completion and a common countable diagonal selection with an atomic covariance criterion ensuring that quantile pushforward preserves the necessary finite-chain factorization even at omitted times. These mechanisms supply a substantive research-level simultaneous process construction, beyond the old existence/minimal-pair-coupling theorem and beyond the low-difficulty continuity lemma.
core_assessment: The dense interval-pair exhaustion and nested finite unions recover every open-interval level kernel; essential atomic times must lie in that common set. The atomic covariance identity then forces one adjacent conditional law constant on each atom interval, so quantile pushforward commutes with the required concatenation. Finite block identification and increasing-kernel continuity give all finite-dimensional limits, with the final atomic argument ensuring the limit stays Markov.
prerequisite_assessment: Only the listed elementary probability/quantile foundations are free. The CDF metric, kernel continuity, common-time choice, level construction and atomic covariance/distributivity arguments remain in the author proof chain.

core_obligations: Construct level kernels L_R as directed lower-orthant limits of finite atomic averaging products, with the composition law needed for a process.
Choose one countable time set simultaneously recovering every open-interval level coupling; separate this obligation from individually chosen approximating sequences for each pair(s,t).

Prove that omitted times cannot be essential atomic times and use the actual atomic interval covariance/distributivity argument to commute quantile pushforward with concatenation. Identify finite Markovizations as pushforwards of finite level processes and obtain convergence of every finite-dimensional marginal to a law that remains Markov after the quantile maps.

proof_roadmap.step: Construct ordered suprema and countable approximations in the lower-orthant CDF order.
Use atomic averaging, decreasing-density tests and composition contraction to construct L_R and the Markov-quantile two-marginals.
Apply a dense-pair diagonal selection and interval exhaustion to obtain one common time set; prove it contains every essential atomic time.

Analyze fitting of a quantile map to conditional kernels. Equality before and after averaging on an atomic interval forces one side to be constant there, yielding the full concatenation pushforward identity.
Prove finite-level/finite-Markovization equality, pass each finite chain to its limit, and use nonessentiality of omitted times plus atomic distributivity to recover the Markov limit.

editorial_notes: This task counts Theorem B in the author stated finite-dimensional convergence sense. No arbitrary dense time set, full path topology, continuous version or strong Markov assertion is claimed. The detailed theorem excerpt stops at(a),(b); its(c) classification is not assumed.

Increasing kernel is used in Proposition3.11(b), printed here. The unused probability-valued monotone extension to every point outside the initial support in3.11(c) is not asserted. All actual level kernels act on[0,1]; general quantile images use almost-sure versions.

The source bounded-density closure wording1095-1104 is used only with a common bound. In1345 a fixed input theta<=M*mu has theta P_n<=M*nu because the target marginal is fixed; thus the required uniform bound is present. No closure claim for arbitrarily unbounded densities is assumed.

At970 the general d-dimensional rectangle increment has the usual sign(-1)^(d-|epsilon|); the printed even-parity convention is correct in dimension2, the dimension of the directed level-coupling construction. At993 the mixed-increment condition must hold for the infimum CDF, as991 and the actual proof1017 explain, not merely for each individual CDF.

At1605 the CDF comparison is reversed in print: the stochastic monotonicity proved1582 gives F[L_R]<=F[L_R-prime] when R-prime subset R, consistent with the stated lower-orthant order1591. Original formulas are retained.

At1817 the finite approximating choices can and must retain the preceding finite set when moving to accuracy n, as required by1811. Equivalently take cumulative finite unions of the displayed choices; monotonicity1804/1591 preserves every approximation. This makes the author intended nested diagonal construction explicit.1876-1877 uses an undefined R-prime_n; the directly preceding1811 approximation and1804 limit already identify the limit for the chosen R_n. Do not infer a common time set from pairwise existence alone.
At1832 the second factor concerns(t,s-prime), as correctly written in the next line1833, not the repeated(s,t) interval. The contradiction remains the author composition/continuity argument.

In the atomic covariance proof,1915 suppresses the Lebesgue factor in the constant-density measure, and1919 reverses its displayed indicator inequality. Both are fixed by1915-1917 and the nonnegative covariance identity. At1957 both lower-orthant kernel test functions are decreasing, not increasing; the same covariance inequality holds for two functions with the same direction, consistently with2062-2063.

The multivariate targets in1925/2054 have the stated coordinate marginals but are not assumed independent. The actual kernel integrals1941-1966 and the chain formula2063 use their full joint laws. The printed tensor-product target notation cannot be read as an extra product-law hypothesis.

In1994-2016, m/n both refer to the number of Markovization times; all blocks B_0,...,B_m are included. The explicit finite endpoint products in2000-2002 determine the block law; the L_[r_k,r_(k+1)] label there is not a replacement by all intervening real times or an identification of two- and three-coordinate laws. At2005 the defining q_r has starting measure lambda, as1454-1456 specifies, not mu_r.2016 ends its interior list atell_k, as correctly written2021, and2051 ends the chain withs_(k-1),s_k.

Original references to the simultaneous two-point/whole-process equality are not treated as proof shortcuts: the full finite-level pushforward argument1990-2036 and the atomic-factorization argument2050-2064 are retained.

Source1375 says the sequence is increasing: the needed and definitionally supplied fact is that each function tilde(h)_n is increasing in its spatial variable, not that n maps to that function is increasing.

The pointwise proof1373-1385 uses [0,1] notation while the concatenation result is on R. Its bounded-coordinate argument transports through any fixed increasing homeomorphism R to(0,1); this ordinary coordinate convention and the already printed quantile transform handle general probability marginals. Independent review must confirm that no substantive missing author argument is concealed by this convention.

At1381 the symmetric lower-limit inequality is printed <=; the symmetric claim needed for convergence is >=, uniquely fixed by the limsup bound being proved and the target conclusion. At1379 the displayed difference of half-line indicators gives[a,b), not[a,b]; either endpoint convention is allowed among monotone test functions, including1_(b,infinity) for the closed version. The originals remain visible.

At1389 the displayed order P-prime circ P reverses the typed concatenation. The defining marginals and actual proof1395,1399 unambiguously use P circ P-prime. At1402 tilde(h)_n means P-prime_n dot h, as the preceding integral1399 explicitly shows. At1435 the repeated index i+i and last n are local index slips determined by the adjacent projection i,i+1 and chain length d. No author formula is silently overwritten.

At1807 the final displayed distance has the finite approximant as its first entry. The initial monotone-metric remark in the same proof directly bounds rho(L_Rtau,L_R) by rho(L_Rprime,L_R); this is the quantity required for convergence. The source order sandwich and proof are retained.
